fields.mechanism: Passive liquid-level stabilization and internal flow-path geometry control in cyclone separators to govern phase separation without active mechanical elements, inverted to use structural boundary-layer management rather than active chemical dosing or moving parts to suppress scale nucleation.
fields.intervention: Install a mechanically clamped, weld-free internal sleeve conforming to the existing vessel geometry that passively reshapes the near-wall velocity profile and maintains a stable liquid film over the separator internals and injection headers, removing the active flashing element from direct wall contact by using the structural surface itself as a passive boundary-layer controller.
fields.expected_effect: The passive liquid film and modified near-wall shear prevent localized supersaturation of calcite and silica gel at the metal surfaces, eliminating the 6 to 11 percent quarterly thermal output loss caused by scale deposition on the cyclone separator internals and downstream headers within the 45 to 60 day window.
fields.falsification_test: Operate the retrofitted wellhead cyclone separator for 90 days and measure the internal mass accumulation rate; if calcite or silica gel deposition exceeds 0.1 mm thickness on the passive sleeve or underlying internals, the mechanism is falsified.
